text:
Korean shares opened higher Thursday after the previous session's sharp decline, as investors remained concerned about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade.
After opening 1.01 percent higher, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) increased 62.07 points, or 1.32 percent, to 4,759.58 as of 9:15 a.m.
On Wednesday, the KOSPI plunged more than 6 percent, reversing the previous session's rally, as an overnight sell-off in technology stocks on Wall Street revived concerns over the sustainability of the AI trade.
Beyond AI-related concerns, investors are also assessing U.S. plans to impose a fresh round of tariffs on goods from 14 countries, including South Korea.
Overnight, U.S. stocks closed mixed, as gains in shares of Anthropic and a recovery in U.S. stocks linked to AI servers, optical communications and power grids helped pare earlier losses.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.33 percent, while the S&P 500 fell 0.25 percent and the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite declined 0.62 percent.
Market bellwether Samsung Electronics added 1.23 percent, while its chipmaking rival SK hynix gained 3.69 percent.
Among other index heavyweights, SK Square, the parent of SK hynix, added 1.89 percent, and power equipment manufacturer Samsung Electro-Mechanics went up 4.9 percent.
The Korean won was quoted at 1,344.3 won against the U.S. dollar as of 9:15 a.m., unchanged from the previous stock trading session's close.
